# `jouet edit`

- **Usage:** `jouet edit [FLAGS] [PATHS]… [SUBCOMMAND]`

Make exact, all-or-nothing edits across files

Reads a spec from --spec or stdin: search/replace blocks, a Codex-style patch, or JSON. Every edit is checked before any file is written, so a failed edit leaves every file as it was.

A SEARCH block holds whole lines, indentation included: one that holds part of a line matches nothing, and the failure says which line the text is inside. `jouet edit replace` matches text anywhere, inside a line too.

A blocks section headed `=== PATH#SYMBOL` replaces a whole definition, found with tree-sitter, so a formatter reflowing its text cannot break the match. SYMBOL is a name, a kind and a name (`fn download`), or a qualified name (`Vfox::download`), as `jouet read FILE --outline` lists them; it must match exactly one definition. The new text runs to the next `===` line, at any indentation: it is indented to where the definition sits. Comments and attributes above the definition stay. An edit that would add syntax errors is refused. When an edit changes the definition's first line, its callers in other files are listed from the code graph (`jouet graph`), or the change is noted when there is none.

  === src/backend/vfox.rs#Vfox::download
  pub fn download(&self, url: &str, retries: u32) -> Result<()> {
      ...
  }

`--pattern PAT --rewrite REPL --lang LANG [PATH...]` rewrites every match of a structural pattern (ast-grep's) under the paths, instead of reading a spec. The rewrites go through the same all-or-nothing writes, --dry-run, --diff, --check and --revert-on-fail, a rewrite that adds syntax errors is refused, and a pattern that matches nothing writes nothing (exit 4). A pattern is code in LANG:

- Quote it in single quotes. In double quotes the shell expands `$X`,
  and `"$X.unwrap()"` becomes `.unwrap()`, which matches nothing.
- `$X` (uppercase) matches exactly one node; `$$$X` matches any number,
  such as all of a call's arguments. `foo($A)` matches only one-argument
  calls, `foo($$$ARGS)` every call. `$_` matches without capturing.
- It must be whole code: `client.get($URL)`, not `get($URL`. A Rust
  call pattern matches the call, not a `?` or `;` after it.
- A name used twice must match the same text twice: `$A == $A`. - REPL is text with the pattern's `$X` filled in; the rest is copied as
  written, and indentation follows the match.

`--callers-of PATH#SYMBOL` rewrites only the calls the code graph attributes to that definition, so `load($$$A)` leaves other functions named `load` alone; write the pattern for the whole call (`$F($P)`, `$R.load($$$A)`). `--impact PATH#SYMBOL` rewrites only inside it and the code depending on it. Matches the graph cannot attribute (dynamic dispatch, macros, files it has not read) are listed as unresolved and left alone, and so are its calls the pattern missed. The report lists each rewrite and the test files that depend on them; --dry-run first.

Examples:
  jouet edit --pattern '$C.get($URL).send()?' --rewrite '$C.get($URL).timeout(TIMEOUT).send()?' --lang rust src/
  jouet edit --pattern 'print($$$ARGS)' --rewrite 'log.info($$$ARGS)' --lang python app/ --check 'python -m pytest -q' --revert-on-fail
  jouet edit --dry-run --pattern '$F($P)' --rewrite '$F($P, None)' --lang rust --callers-of src/config.rs#load

Try a pattern with `jouet search --structural --lang LANG 'PAT'` first.

## Arguments
- **`[PATHS]…`** — With --pattern, the files and directories to rewrite (default .)

## Global Flags
- **`--dry-run`** — Report what would change without writing anything
- **`--diff`** — Include a unified diff of each changed file
- **`--check <CMD>`** — Run CMD through the shell after writing
- **`--diag`** — Fail if the edit introduced diagnostics: the edited files are checked through hk (`jouet diag`) before and after writing, and only new findings count
- **`--revert-on-fail`** — Restore every edited file if --check or --diag fails
- **`--why`** — Warn when the edit changes lines an earlier agent session wrote, by `entire why`: the session, checkpoint and prompt behind them, so `--dry-run --why` shows it before anything is written. It warns and does not refuse. Needs Entire enabled in the repository; off by default because `entire why` can take a minute where the history is long. Looks at the first 10 files
- **`--expect-hash <PATH=SHA256>`** — Refuse unless PATH's contents have this SHA-256 hash. Repeatable

## Flags
- **`--spec <FILE>`** — Read the spec from FILE instead of stdin (`-` is stdin)
- **`--format <FORMAT>`** — Spec format: blocks, patch or json. Detected from the first line
- **`--pattern <PAT>`** — Rewrite code matching this ast-grep pattern, instead of reading a spec
- **`--rewrite <REPL>`** — What --pattern's matches become; its `$X` are the pattern's
- **`--lang <LANG>`** — The language of --pattern: rust, python, javascript, typescript, tsx, go, ruby, java, c or cpp
- **`--callers-of <PATH#SYMBOL>`** — With --pattern, rewrite only the calls the code graph attributes to this symbol, given as PATH#NAME (or #ID from `jouet graph symbols`)
- **`--impact <PATH#SYMBOL>`** — With --pattern, rewrite only inside this symbol and the code the graph says depends on it, three hops back
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
